title: Windows Terminal AI Workspace Setup
summary: Create and verify a disposable Git workspace in a dedicated Windows Terminal PowerShell profile, with a separately labelled optional WSL branch and safe recovery steps.
prerequisites: Windows Terminal installed through a Microsoft-supported channel

sections.title: Understand the boundaries and minimum requirements
paragraphs: Windows Terminal is the host application. A profile tells that host which shell executable to start and where it should start. PowerShell is the required shell for the main branch. Git is a separate command-line program. WSL, used only in the optional branch, supplies a Linux runtime with Linux users and paths. A successful check in one shell or runtime does not prove that the same program exists in another.

This guide requires Windows Terminal, a working PowerShell executable available as powershell.exe, and Git available in that same PowerShell environment. No specific minimum Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or Git release can be stated from the supplied primary sources. The operational minimum is therefore feature-based: Windows Terminal must accept a profile with name, commandline, and startingDirectory; PowerShell must run the commands below; and Git must support init and status. Do not continue if any check fails.

For the optional WSL installation command, Microsoft's stated minimum is Windows 10 version 2004, build 19041, or Windows 11. Installation must be performed in an administrator PowerShell window and followed by a computer restart. WSL installation and elevation are not required for the main Windows and PowerShell branch.

This lesson does not install an AI tool, paid model service, or credential. Never place tokens, passwords, or other secrets in settings.json. Commands in this lesson create or inspect only a new directory named Project42-Terminal-Practice and its new Git repository. They do not clone or modify an existing repository.

code.label: Main-branch prerequisite and version checks in PowerShell
code.code:
$PSVersionTable.PSVersion
git --version
wt --help

sections.title: Interpret the prerequisite checks without inventing version output
paragraphs: Run the three checks in an existing PowerShell session. Expected output is machine-dependent. The PowerShell expression should display a version object with fields such as Major and Minor. The Git command should print a line beginning with git version. The Terminal command should display Windows Terminal command-line help. Record the actual values shown by your computer rather than copying an example number.

If powershell.exe cannot be launched, install or repair a Microsoft-supported PowerShell or Windows PowerShell installation before continuing. If git is not recognized, install Git through your organization's approved source, close and reopen Terminal, and repeat git --version. The supplied sources do not establish a minimum Git version or an installation command, so this resource does not invent one. If wt is not recognized, install or repair Windows Terminal through a Microsoft-supported channel and verify its execution alias. Do not edit settings until all three main-branch checks work.

If you already have a directory named Project42-Terminal-Practice under your Windows user profile, stop. Preserve it and use the learner variation later, whose distinct directory name is Project42-Terminal-Lab. None of the commands below may be used against an existing directory or repository.

code.label: Fail safely if the worked-example directory already exists

sections.title: Create the supplied disposable Windows practice repository
paragraphs: This is the fully supplied practice repository: a new local Git repository at %USERPROFILE%\Project42-Terminal-Practice. It does not require a remote URL or network access. The commands first refuse to proceed if that path exists, then create the directory, initialize Git, and create one untracked practice file. Creating an untracked file gives git status a visible, read-only result without requiring Git identity configuration or a commit.

Run this block only in PowerShell. Expected output is machine-dependent. New-Item should report a newly created directory, git init should report initialization of an empty Git repository and show a path ending in Project42-Terminal-Practice\.git, and git status should identify an untracked file named workspace-note.txt. Git may use different wording or an initial branch name. The status command itself is read-only.

code.label: Create only the new Windows practice artifacts
code.code:
$Practice = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Project42-Terminal-Practice'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Practice) { throw "STOP: $Practice already exists. Nothing was changed." }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Practice
Set-Location -LiteralPath $Practice
git init
Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Practice 'workspace-note.txt') -Value 'Project 42 disposable terminal practice repository.'
git status

sections.title: Insert one complete profile object into settings.json
paragraphs: Open Windows Terminal Settings, then choose Open JSON file. This opens the settings.json used by that Terminal installation without requiring you to guess a package path. Before editing, use Save As in the editor to make a backup named settings.before-project42.json beside settings.json. The backup must not contain newly added credentials, and this profile contains none.

Find the root-level profiles object, then find its list array. Insert the complete object below as one new element inside profiles.list. If another object follows it, add a comma after the new object's closing brace. If an object precedes it, ensure that preceding object already ends with a comma. Do not place the object in profiles.defaults, do not place it at the root, and never replace the complete settings file. If profiles.list is absent, do not invent that JSON structure or paste the displayed fragment over the file. Instead, use Windows Terminal Settings, choose Add a new profile and New empty profile, enter the supplied Name, Command line, and Starting directory values, then save through the Settings UI. The profile name is the launch identifier. The commandline starts Windows PowerShell, and the Windows starting directory resolves to the new practice directory.

The displayed fragment includes surrounding structure only to make the merge location precise. Keep every existing root property, every existing profiles.defaults setting, and every existing profiles.list item. Copy only the marked profile object into the existing list. A root-level defaultProfile is required by Windows Terminal settings and accepts a GUID or profile name, but this lesson does not change it. Launching the new profile explicitly is safer than changing the learner's default.

code.label: Complete profile object shown at its exact merge location

sections.title: Launch and verify the Windows PowerShell workspace
paragraphs: Save settings.json, close the settings editor, and run the startup command below from PowerShell. Windows Terminal's wt new-tab command accepts a named profile and a starting directory. The command repeats the directory explicitly so both the selected profile and launch path are testable. No semicolon escaping is needed because this command opens one tab. For multi-command wt invocations in PowerShell, semicolons used by wt must be escaped with backticks.

In the newly opened tab, run the verification block. Expected output is machine-dependent. The version expression should produce a PowerShell version object. Get-Location should end with Project42-Terminal-Practice. $env:OS should normally identify the Windows_NT environment for this Windows PowerShell profile. Get-Command git should resolve a Git command available to this shell. git rev-parse should print the full path of the supplied practice repository, and git status should identify workspace-note.txt as untracked unless the learner intentionally changed the new repository. Do not claim success until the fresh tab supplies this evidence.

code.label: Startup command from PowerShell
code.code: wt new-tab -p "Project42 PowerShell Practice" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice"

sections.title: Collect shell, path, executable, and read-only Git evidence
paragraphs: These checks distinguish the Terminal host from its shell and distinguish a Windows path from a Linux path. Get-Process inspects the current shell process name. It should indicate powershell for the configured powershell.exe commandline. Get-Location verifies the Windows working directory. Git resolution and repository-root checks must be run inside this same fresh profile, not in the old setup tab.
The final git status is the required read-only Git check. It reads repository state and should show the untracked practice file. It does not stage, commit, reset, clean, or delete anything.

code.label: Verification inside the fresh Project42 PowerShell Practice tab
code.code:
$PSVersionTable.PSVersion
(Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName
Get-Location
$env:OS
Get-Command git
git --version
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status

sections.title: Worked successful setup and expected evidence
paragraphs: Worked example sequence: the learner passes the PowerShell, Git, and wt checks; confirms that %USERPROFILE%\Project42-Terminal-Practice does not exist; creates that directory; initializes the local repository; writes workspace-note.txt; inserts only the Project42 PowerShell Practice object into profiles.list; saves settings.json; and launches the named profile with wt. The fresh tab starts powershell.exe in the practice directory.

Expected evidence, all machine-dependent: the shell process name indicates powershell; the location and Git top-level path both end in Project42-Terminal-Practice; git --version begins with git version followed by the installed machine's version; and git status reports the repository state with workspace-note.txt under untracked files. The exact user path, drive, PowerShell version, Git version, branch name, spacing, and wording vary by machine. This is a worked procedure and expected pattern, not a claim that these commands were executed.

code.label: Machine-dependent success pattern, not captured execution
code.code:
PowerShell version: version object; exact numbers vary
Shell process: powershell
Location: ...\Project42-Terminal-Practice
OS marker: Windows_NT
Git command: resolves in this PowerShell session
Git version: git version <machine-dependent version>
Repository root: ...\Project42-Terminal-Practice
Git status: repository status plus untracked workspace-note.txt

sections.title: Diagnose and recover from a deliberate wrong path or profile
paragraphs: Deliberate failure exercise: from the original PowerShell tab, open a plain PowerShell profile at the Windows user home with the first command below. This is intentionally the wrong launch because it does not select Project42 PowerShell Practice and explicitly starts in %USERPROFILE%. Run the diagnosis block only. Expected machine-dependent evidence is that Get-Location shows the user home rather than Project42-Terminal-Practice. git rev-parse will usually report that the location is not a Git repository, unless the learner's home is already inside a Git work tree. In that exceptional case, its printed root still will not equal the named practice repository. No file is changed.

Recover reversibly by closing only the deliberately wrong tab, or leave it open and run the recovery launch command from PowerShell. Then repeat the verification block in the correctly named profile. If Terminal reports that the profile cannot be found, reopen settings.json, check that the object is inside profiles.list and that its name matches exactly, correct only that new object, save, and retry. If the directory cannot be found, verify that Test-Path for the exact practice path returns True and restore the object's startingDirectory exactly as supplied.

If settings fail to load after the edit, close Terminal, open the settings file through the same Settings interface if available, compare it with settings.before-project42.json, and remove only the newly inserted Project42 profile object while preserving valid JSON commas. If manual repair is unclear, restore the beside-file backup as settings.json only after preserving the broken file under a different diagnostic name. This recovery reverts the learner's own immediately preceding settings change and must not be used to replace unrelated settings backups.

code.label: Deliberately launch the wrong profile and path, then diagnose
code.code:
wt new-tab -p "Windows PowerShell" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE"
# Run these in the deliberately wrong tab:
(Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName
Get-Location
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status

sections.title: Reopen the intended profile after diagnosis
paragraphs: This command is the reversible recovery from the deliberate wrong tab. It selects the intended profile and path without changing the default profile or any repository content.

code.label: Recovery launch command
code.code: wt new-tab -p "Project42 PowerShell Practice" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice"

sections.title: Optional WSL branch: install, discover, and verify Linux separately
paragraphs: This entire section is optional and separate from the Windows PowerShell setup. Skip installation if wsl --list --verbose already lists a distribution. If WSL is absent and the computer meets Microsoft's requirement of Windows 10 version 2004, build 19041 or higher, or Windows 11, open PowerShell with Run as administrator, run wsl --install, and restart the computer. The command enables required features and installs Ubuntu by default. On first launch, complete the Linux user-account setup. Do not put that Linux password or any credential in Terminal settings.

After restart, use a normal, non-administrator PowerShell window for discovery. wsl --list --verbose displays installed distribution names, state, and WSL version. Its values are machine-dependent. This guide's concrete optional example requires a distribution whose listed name is exactly Ubuntu. If the installed name differs, do not invent or substitute a distribution name in a command. Continue with the supplied Ubuntu commands only after a distribution named Ubuntu exists. You may set an installed Ubuntu distribution as the default with wsl --set-default Ubuntu, but changing the default is optional.

If wsl is not recognized, confirm the Windows requirement, perform the administrator installation and restart, then retry. If no distribution is listed after WSL itself is available, run wsl --list --online and install the concrete Ubuntu choice with wsl --install -d Ubuntu from administrator PowerShell if organizational policy allows, then restart if prompted and complete first-launch setup. If Git is absent inside Ubuntu, stop the WSL Git portion. Installing Git inside Linux is distribution-specific and no supplied primary source establishes that installation command.

A WSL profile is still hosted by Windows Terminal, but its shell and filesystem semantics are Linux. The Linux practice repository below lives at ~/Project42-WSL-Practice, not in the Windows repository and not under a C:\ path. Run the Linux block only after entering Ubuntu. It refuses to change an existing path, creates a new Linux directory, initializes a separate Git repository, and creates one untracked file.

code.label: Administrator PowerShell only when WSL or Ubuntu must be installed
code.code:
wsl --install
# Restart Windows after installation. If WSL exists but Ubuntu is absent:
wsl --list --online
wsl --install -d Ubuntu

sections.title: Discover WSL from normal PowerShell
paragraphs: Run these commands after any required restart. Expected output is machine-dependent. The list should include a NAME column, a STATE column, and a VERSION column. Continue with this guide's fixed Ubuntu example only if NAME includes Ubuntu. The status and version commands report configuration and component versions supported by the installed WSL command.

code.label: Normal PowerShell WSL discovery and checks
code.code:
wsl --list --verbose
wsl --status
wsl --version

sections.title: Create and verify the separate Linux practice repository
paragraphs: Start Ubuntu from normal PowerShell with wsl --distribution Ubuntu, then run this Bash block inside the Linux shell. Expected output is machine-dependent. pwd should initially show a Linux home path of the form /home/<Linux-user>. whoami prints the actual Linux username. git --version starts with git version if Git is installed in Ubuntu. After creation, pwd and git rev-parse should end in /Project42-WSL-Practice, and git status should identify workspace-note.txt as untracked.

The mkdir command is guarded by a directory-existence test. It does not reuse or delete an existing directory. The printf command writes only the newly named file inside the newly confirmed-absent directory.

code.label: Run inside the Ubuntu Linux shell, not PowerShell
code.code:
pwd
whoami
git --version
if [ -e "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice" ]; then
  echo "STOP: $HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice already exists. Nothing was changed."
  return 1 2>/dev/null || exit 1
fi
mkdir "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice"
cd "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice"
git init
printf '%s\n' 'Project 42 disposable WSL terminal practice repository.' > workspace-note.txt
pwd
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status

sections.title: Launch Ubuntu through its dynamic profile or WSL command
paragraphs: Windows Terminal automatically generates dynamic profiles for installed WSL distributions when the Windows.Terminal.Wsl profile source is enabled. After wsl --list --verbose confirms an installed distribution named exactly Ubuntu, inspect the Terminal profile menu. If it contains a profile named Ubuntu, the first command below launches that named dynamic profile. Do not add a manual WSL profile object, do not construct a Linux home path with %USERNAME%, and do not overwrite settings.json.

Run exactly one of the two startup commands from normal PowerShell. Use wt new-tab -p "Ubuntu" only when the Terminal profile menu shows that exact profile name. Otherwise, use wsl --distribution Ubuntu. The second command directly launches the installed distribution named Ubuntu and does not depend on a manually configured Terminal profile or a Windows username. After either command opens the Linux shell, use the next section's cd command to enter ~/Project42-WSL-Practice.

code.label: Choose one supported Ubuntu launch method from normal PowerShell
code.code:
# If Windows Terminal shows a dynamic profile named exactly Ubuntu:
wt new-tab -p "Ubuntu"

# Otherwise, launch the installed distribution directly instead:
wsl --distribution Ubuntu

sections.title: Enter the optional WSL workspace without assuming usernames match
paragraphs: Windows and Linux usernames can differ. The Windows %USERNAME% environment variable therefore must not be used to identify the Linux home directory. After launching Ubuntu by either supported method in the preceding section, run the command below inside the Ubuntu Linux shell. $HOME is resolved by that Linux shell for its current Linux user, so no Windows username or machine-specific literal path is required.

Expected output is machine-dependent. pwd should end with /Project42-WSL-Practice. If cd reports that the directory does not exist, stop and return to the create-wsl-practice section. Do not invent a username or create a replacement directory during verification. The next section supplies the complete Linux shell and Git checks.

code.label: Run inside the launched Ubuntu Linux shell
code.code:
cd "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice"
pwd

sections.title: Verify the Linux shell and repository
paragraphs: Run this block only inside Ubuntu. It checks the Linux home path, shell process, executable resolution, repository root, and read-only status without assuming a Windows path.

code.label: Verification inside Ubuntu
code.code:
cd "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice"
pwd
ps -p $$ -o comm=
command -v git
git --version
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status

sections.title: Learner variation: build a second Windows profile and repository
paragraphs: Create a second, separate Windows practice repository named Project42-Terminal-Lab and a profile named Project42 PowerShell Lab. Do not alter the worked-example repository or profile. Your task is to: safely refuse an existing lab path; create the new directory; initialize Git; create lab-note.txt containing Project 42 learner variation; add the supplied profile object to profiles.list when that array exists, or use the earlier Add a new profile and New empty profile Settings UI procedure when it does not; launch it explicitly; and verify shell, location, Git resolution, repository root, and read-only status.

Use only the two exact names and the exact file content supplied here. Keep the exercise in Windows PowerShell. Do not use WSL, do not change defaultProfile, and do not replace settings.json. Complete the task before reading the separate answer key.

code.label: Fixed learner-variation inputs
code.code:
Directory: %USERPROFILE%\Project42-Terminal-Lab
Profile name: Project42 PowerShell Lab
Shell commandline: powershell.exe
File: lab-note.txt
File content: Project 42 learner variation

sections.title: Separate explained answer key
paragraphs: The guard makes the exercise safe by stopping before any write if the lab directory already exists. New-Item creates only the named directory, git init creates only its .git metadata, and Set-Content creates only lab-note.txt inside that new directory. The first git status is read-only and should show lab-note.txt as untracked.

Merge the answer-key profile object into profiles.list using the earlier backup and comma instructions. The startup command selects that profile by exact name and repeats its exact Windows directory. In the fresh tab, the location and repository root should end in Project42-Terminal-Lab, the process should indicate powershell, Git should resolve, and git status should show the untracked lab-note.txt. Exact versions and paths remain machine-dependent.

code.label: Answer key part 1: safely create the learner-variation repository
code.code:
$Lab = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Project42-Terminal-Lab'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Lab) { throw "STOP: $Lab already exists. Nothing was changed." }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Lab
Set-Location -LiteralPath $Lab
git init
Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Lab 'lab-note.txt') -Value 'Project 42 learner variation'
git status

sections.title: Answer key profile and launch
paragraphs: If profiles.list exists, insert only this complete object into that array and save the existing file rather than replacing it. If profiles.list is absent, do not invent JSON structure. Use Windows Terminal Settings, choose Add a new profile and New empty profile, and enter the same Name, Command line, and Starting directory values through the UI. Then launch from PowerShell.

code.label: Answer key part 2: complete lab profile object

sections.title: Answer key verification
paragraphs: Run the startup line in PowerShell, then run the remaining lines in the fresh lab tab. Expected output is machine-dependent and follows the patterns explained above.

code.label: Answer key part 3: launch and verify
code.code:
wt new-tab -p "Project42 PowerShell Lab" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Lab"
# Run the following in the fresh lab tab:
(Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName
Get-Location
Get-Command git
git --version
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status

sections.title: Clean up only the named new practice artifacts
paragraphs: Cleanup is optional. Close tabs using the practice profiles. In settings.json, delete only the complete profile objects named Project42 PowerShell Practice and Project42 PowerShell Lab if you added them through JSON. Repair only the adjacent commas needed to keep profiles.list valid. If you created either Windows profile through the Settings UI, remove only that named profile through the same UI. The optional WSL branch uses the installed Ubuntu dynamic profile or wsl --distribution Ubuntu and adds no Project42 WSL profile to remove. Do not delete other profiles, do not replace the settings file, and do not change defaultProfile.

File cleanup must be limited to directories created by this lesson. Before deletion, inspect each exact path and confirm it is the intended disposable repository. This resource intentionally supplies no recursive deletion command because a mistyped or repurposed path could destroy data. Use File Explorer for the two Windows directories and delete them only after verifying their names and contents. For the optional Linux directory, inspect it with pwd and ls -la, then remove its files and directory manually only if it remains the disposable artifact. Never run cleanup against an existing user repository, and never unregister a WSL distribution.

The settings.before-project42.json backup is also a named practice artifact. Delete it only after the profiles have been removed, settings.json loads correctly, and you have confirmed it is the backup created by this lesson.

code.label: Read-only pre-cleanup inspection for Windows artifacts
code.code:
Get-Item -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ChildItem -Force -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-Item -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Lab" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ChildItem -Force -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Lab" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

sections.title: ASSUMPTIONS.
paragraphs: The preserved metadata comes from the supplied canonical original. The main branch assumes powershell.exe is the learner's supported shell because the work item specifically requests a Windows Terminal plus PowerShell setup. It assumes Windows Terminal's Settings interface exposes Open JSON file and that the learner can save a beside-file backup with their editor. The local, newly initialized repositories are treated as the fully supplied practice repositories because no remote repository URL was supplied and network access is unnecessary.

The optional WSL example assumes a distribution named Ubuntu only after discovery or explicit installation of Ubuntu. Linux usernames are machine-dependent and are not assumed to equal Windows usernames. The WSL launch procedure uses either the installed distribution's dynamic Terminal profile or wsl --distribution Ubuntu, followed by a Linux-shell cd using $HOME. No command in this resource is claimed to have been executed.

sections.title: OMITTED.
paragraphs: No minimum numeric Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or Git versions are stated because the supplied primary sources do not establish them. No Git installation command is supplied because the research findings provide no fetched primary installation source for Git. No destructive cleanup command is supplied because the acceptance criteria prohibit risking an existing repository; cleanup is instead constrained to inspected, named artifacts through manual deletion.

No manual Project42 WSL profile object or literal WSL startingDirectory is supplied because the Linux username is machine-dependent and Windows %USERNAME% does not reliably identify it. The supported procedure instead launches the installed Ubuntu distribution through its named dynamic profile or wsl --distribution Ubuntu, then changes directory inside Linux with cd "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice". Nothing else requested by the work item is omitted.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: This section records evidence for the existing Windows Terminal setup. It does not report that any command was executed. A Windows setup passes only after the learner interactively confirms the prerequisite checks, creates the new repository, saves the existing settings.json with the supplied Project42 PowerShell Practice profile object, launches a fresh tab, and observes the verification results in that tab.

Windows pass evidence is machine-dependent in exact version numbers, drive letters, usernames, branch names, and command wording. The fresh tab should run powershell.exe, Get-Location should end in Project42-Terminal-Practice, $env:OS should identify Windows_NT, Get-Command git should resolve Git, git rev-parse --show-toplevel should resolve to the same Project42-Terminal-Practice repository, and git status should report workspace-note.txt as untracked. A failed prerequisite, a missing profile, a different shell, a different directory, an unresolved Git command, a different repository root, or missing workspace-note.txt is fail evidence until diagnosed.

The profile edit requires interactive confirmation in Windows Terminal Settings or its Open JSON file workflow. The learner must confirm that the complete existing settings file was preserved, that the supplied object is inside profiles.list, that its name is exactly Project42 PowerShell Practice, and that settings.json still loads. The guide does not change defaultProfile. These profile and startup behaviors are documented by Microsoft at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/terminal/customize-settings/profile-general and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/terminal/command-line-arguments.

Recovery for the Windows branch is limited to the learner's new artifacts and the immediately preceding profile edit. If the wrong tab opens, close that tab or run the existing recovery command, then repeat verification in the fresh Project42 PowerShell Practice tab. If the profile is missing, inspect the existing settings.json and correct only the newly inserted object. If settings.json fails to load, preserve the broken file under a diagnostic name, compare it with settings.before-project42.json, and remove only the new profile object while preserving valid JSON commas and all unrelated settings. Do not replace unrelated settings or delete an existing repository.

The optional WSL branch is separate from Windows completion. WSL is not required for a passing Windows setup. If the learner elects to verify WSL, interactive confirmation is required for the Windows version requirement, administrator elevation, any restart after wsl --install, Ubuntu first-launch account setup, and the distribution name returned by wsl --list --verbose. The supplied Ubuntu commands must be run inside the Ubuntu Linux shell, not in PowerShell.

Optional WSL pass evidence is machine-dependent but should show a Linux shell, a working Git command inside Ubuntu, pwd ending in /Project42-WSL-Practice, git rev-parse --show-toplevel ending in the same Linux repository, and git status reporting workspace-note.txt as untracked. The Windows repository and the Linux repository are separate. A missing Ubuntu distribution, a failed WSL installation, a missing Linux Git command, a Windows path used as the Linux workspace, or verification performed in PowerShell is fail evidence for the optional branch only. Microsoft's WSL installation and command references are https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/basic-commands.
No execution, test run, successful setup, or observed output is claimed here. Only the learner's interactive confirmation on the target computer can establish pass or fail.

code.label: Operational acceptance, verification, and recovery fields
code.code:
Task: Confirm the existing Windows Terminal setup by checking PowerShell, Git, and wt; safely create %USERPROFILE%\Project42-Terminal-Practice; initialize Git; create workspace-note.txt; insert the existing Project42 PowerShell Practice profile object into profiles.list without replacing settings.json; launch wt new-tab -p "Project42 PowerShell Practice" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice"; then verify the fresh tab. Optionally verify the separate Ubuntu branch with wsl --list --verbose, wsl --distribution Ubuntu, and the existing Linux practice commands.

Scope: Main branch only changes the new directory %USERPROFILE%\Project42-Terminal-Practice, its .git directory, workspace-note.txt, and the one named Project42 PowerShell Practice profile. The optional branch uses the separate Linux path ~/Project42-WSL-Practice and does not modify the Windows repository or require a Project42 WSL profile.

Permissions: Run the Windows prerequisite, repository, launch, and verification commands in PowerShell. Use Windows Terminal Settings interactively to open settings.json and save settings.before-project42.json beside it before editing. Use administrator PowerShell only for wsl --install or wsl --install -d Ubuntu, then restart if prompted. Use a normal PowerShell window for WSL discovery and launch, and run Linux repository commands inside Ubuntu. Do not place credentials in settings.json.

Verification: In the fresh Windows tab run:
$PSVersionTable.PSVersion
(Get-Process -Id $PID).ProcessName
Get-Location
$env:OS
Get-Command git
git --version
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status
Pass evidence is powershell, a location and repository root ending in Project42-Terminal-Practice, Windows_NT, Git resolution, and untracked workspace-note.txt. For the optional Ubuntu branch, run inside Ubuntu:
cd "$HOME/Project42-WSL-Practice"
pwd
ps -p $$ -o comm=
command -v git
git --version
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status
Pass evidence is a Linux shell, a path and repository root ending in /Project42-WSL-Practice, Git resolution, and untracked workspace-note.txt. Exact output remains machine-dependent.

Recovery: If the intended Windows profile is not selected, close the wrong tab or run:
wt new-tab -p "Project42 PowerShell Practice" --startingDirectory "$env:USERPROFILE\Project42-Terminal-Practice"
If the practice directory already exists, stop and preserve it. If settings.json does not load, preserve the broken file under a diagnostic name, compare it with settings.before-project42.json, and remove only the newly added Project42 PowerShell Practice object while preserving valid JSON commas and unrelated settings. For the optional WSL branch, do not substitute a distribution name, delete the Linux directory, or unregister a distribution. If Ubuntu or the Linux practice path is unavailable, stop and return to the existing discovery and creation instructions.
